requirements.statement: Action-specific authority evaluation is bound to explicit action, resource, evaluation time, material constraints, and a stable action binding when substitution or replay is possible.
Identity, authentication, registration, discovery, capability advertisement, signature verification, or successful resolution alone establish action authority.
Affirmative evaluation requires current effective authority and preserves all material scope, prohibition, temporal, value, resource, purpose, counterparty, jurisdiction, and delegation limits.
Required approvals are bound to the exact action or canonical action digest and are current and verifiable at evaluation time.
Expired, revoked, stale, conflicting, unavailable, unverifiable, or indeterminate material authority or approval state produces an affirmative result.
Collective-principal evaluation uses current membership/controller evidence and the current exercise rule.
An individual member is inferred to independently possess collective authority solely from collective membership.
The same controller is counted more than once toward a threshold unless the governing rule explicitly defines and evidence proves separately exercisable roles.
Missing material membership or collective-rule evidence remains indeterminate.
Execution under a materially different action context requires reevaluation or policy-proven equivalence.
